title: Go Pal Blends American and Indian Aisles in 50,000-Square-Foot Edison Store
excerpt: The hybrid supermarket pairs a full American grocery with an Indian Kitchen serving snacks, entrées and rotis, filling the Edison anchor left vacant since Stop & Shop closed in late 2024.
body:
• Go Pal Supermarket held its grand opening on October 31 at 1083 Inman Ave. in Edison, New Jersey, in the roughly 50,000-square-foot former Stop & Shop at Inman Grove Shopping Center.
  • The store pairs a full American supermarket with an extensive Indian range, including a dedicated Indian Kitchen serving snacks, freshly prepared entrées and rotis.
  • Owner Nick Patel designed the hybrid for multigenerational families and young professionals; the store is open 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily, with online and phone ordering, delivery and pickup.
  • Patel hopes to open two more stores elsewhere in New Jersey in the coming months, though no sites or dates have been announced.

Edison's newest supermarket is built for households that shop two food cultures in one trip. Go Pal Supermarket, a member of the Allegiance Retail Services cooperative, celebrated its grand opening on October 31 in Edison, New Jersey, bringing together traditional American grocery offerings and an extensive selection of Indian foods in an approximately 50,000-square-foot store at 1083 Inman Ave., according to The Shelby Report. Owner Nick Patel cut the ribbon, and Edison Mayor Sam Joshi attended the opening.

"Go Pal Supermarket introduces a hybrid American and Indian grocery concept designed to meet the shopping needs of multigenerational families, young professionals and the surrounding community."

— Nick Patel, owner of Go Pal

What Is Inside

The centrepiece for Indian shoppers is a dedicated Indian Kitchen, featuring traditional Indian snacks, freshly prepared entrées and rotis, alongside an extensive assortment of Indian groceries, ingredients and specialty products. Around it sits a full-service American supermarket: natural and organic products, fresh produce, breads and rolls baked from scratch daily, a full-service deli with prepared foods, fresh sushi, meat and seafood counters, grab-and-go meals, a floral department, full-service catering and the Best Yet private-label line.

Beyond food, the store carries baby products, beauty and personal care items, health and wellness products, household supplies and pet products. Shoppers can order online or by phone — the store's site is go-pal.us — with home delivery and pickup available, and the store runs a loyalty programme and participates in applicable food assistance programmes. Hours are 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily.

"Go Pal is another great example of how our independent grocers are responding to the unique needs and preferences of the communities they serve," said Samer Rahman, president and COO of Allegiance Retail Services, adding that the cooperative was proud to support a store reflecting Edison's Indian culture. Iselin, New Jersey-based Allegiance supports independent supermarket operators with merchandising, marketing, advertising, technology and operations services through its cooperative structure.

A Vacant Anchor, Filled

The store occupies renovated space that formerly housed a Stop & Shop at the 113,000-square-foot, Levin Management-operated Inman Grove Shopping Center. That anchor had stood empty since the chain shuttered 32 underperforming locations across the Northeast in late 2024, ten of them in New Jersey. For residents of that section of North Edison, the opening restores a full-service supermarket to a centre that had lacked one for nearly two years.

Why It Matters for the Diaspora

Edison and the surrounding Middlesex County corridor are home to one of the largest Indian-American communities in the United States, and the hybrid format answers a familiar friction: a weekly shop that previously meant two stops — an American supermarket for household staples and an Indian grocer for produce, spices, snacks and fresh rotis. Go Pal puts both under one roof, with the Indian Kitchen adding ready-to-eat options for families who want a cooked meal from the same trip. Patel told NJ.com he hopes to open two additional stores elsewhere in New Jersey in the coming months after the Edison debut, although specific sites and timelines were not disclosed.
